title: How Bipolar Disorder Works
summary: Josh and Chuck explain bipolar disorder: its prevalence, typical onset in the teens and twenties, the manic and depressive symptoms, mixed and rapid-cycling episodes, the bipolar I, II, and cyclothymia classifications and how the DSM-5 changed them, suspected causes (genetics, brain chemistry, neurotransmitters, triggers like drugs, alcohol, and sleep disruption), medications (lithium, anticonvulsants, antipsychotics, benzodiazepines), non-drug therapies, the link to creativity with famous artists, a first-person account from a Slate essay by Mills Baker, and a listener mail correction about shark gills.

segments.title: Opening banter and personal experiences
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck open with a Squarespace sponsor read, then discuss personal experience knowing people with bipolar disorder and the basic idea of extreme mood swings. They note prevalence figures and that onset is often in the mid-teens to mid-twenties.

segments.title: Manic and depressive symptoms
segments.summary: They describe manic episodes (high energy, rapid speech, euphoria or irritability, risky behavior, psychotic symptoms) and depressive episodes, plus mixed episodes and hypomania. They discuss DSM-5 changes to the episode duration threshold and define rapid cycling.

segments.title: Types of bipolar disorder
segments.summary: They distinguish bipolar I, bipolar II, the former bipolar disorder not otherwise specified category, and cyclothymia, and discuss how DSM-5 criteria were adjusted for adolescents.

segments.title: Causes and brain chemistry
segments.summary: The hosts say the cause is not fully known. Genetics, environmental triggers, and brain chemistry such as serotonin and dopamine imbalances are discussed, with the idea of a baseline range of normal brain chemistry.

segments.title: Medications and treatment approaches
segments.summary: They cover lithium as the go-to mood stabilizer since the 1970s, plus anticonvulsants, antipsychotics, and benzodiazepines, and note that drug choice is trial-and-error with blood-level monitoring. They discuss the debate over living without medication and the role of sleep and dark therapy.

segments.title: Non-medication therapies
segments.summary: They list therapies used alone or alongside medication: cognitive behavioral therapy, family and group therapy, electroconvulsive therapy (referencing an earlier episode), and social rhythm therapy. They emphasize learning triggers and maintaining routines.

segments.title: Bipolar disorder and creativity
segments.summary: They discuss the long-debated link between creativity and bipolar disorder, naming artists said to have had it, including Brian Wilson and the Beach Boys' Smile episode, and note that these accounts predate lithium.

segments.title: First-person account and Slate essay
segments.summary: Chuck reads from a Slate essay by Mills Baker describing how bipolar feels: intense mood cycles that shape personality, distrust of one's own emotional reactions, and life after diagnosis with medication and sleep hygiene. Josh adds a plug for John Ronson's book The Psychopath Test.

segments.title: Listener mail and sign-off
segments.summary: A listener mail about new research published in Nature showing shark gill systems have evolved, correcting the idea that sharks barely changed. Josh and Chuck sign off with contact information.
